meta.question: Can a free Colab/Kaggle datacenter GPU run WebGPU/WGSL after all? (Re-test of FREE_COMPUTE.md §3, which closed it 2026-06-08.)
meta.method: On a Colab T4 GPU runtime: install libnvidia-gl-<driver_major> (the NVIDIA Vulkan producer the 2026-06-08 probe never installed) + register a Vulkan ICD pointing at libGLX_nvidia.so.0, then measure the wgpu-py adapter and compile the real shipped shaders (primary/secondary/chemistry, assembled exactly like src/shaders/loader.ts). Script: kaggle/colab_webgpu_smoke.py; notebook: kaggle/webgpu_dna_colab.ipynb.

honest_scope: This is shader COMPILE + a trivial compute dispatch on the real T4 — NOT a full physics numeric validation. The marquee Phase A+B physics still needs the buffer/pipeline/dispatch host (src/gpu/{buffers,pipelines,dispatch}.ts) ported to Python; that work is now unblocked.
supersedes: The 2026-06-08 probe (FREE_COMPUTE.md §3) reported llvmpipe/CPU/OpenGL and concluded 'datacenter GPUs cannot run our physics'. That was incomplete: it only DETECTED an ICD; it never installed libnvidia-gl-<driver>, so the Vulkan producer library was absent. With it installed, the T4 is Vulkan-visible.
recipe: drv=$(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader | cut -d. -f1); apt-get install -y libnvidia-gl-$drv; echo '{"file_format_version":"1.0.0","ICD":{"library_path":"libGLX_nvidia.so.0","api_version":"1.3.0"}}' > /usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.json; wgpu.gpu.request_adapter_sync(power_preference='high-performance')
reproduce: Open kaggle/webgpu_dna_colab.ipynb in Colab with a GPU (T4) runtime and Run all, or: !git clone -b <branch> https://github.com/abgnydn/webgpu-dna && python webgpu-dna/kaggle/colab_webgpu_smoke.py
